source.title: Cloudflare outage caused by bad software deploy (updated)
source.use_scope: factual summary and attribution; no full article reproduction

official_facts.summary: The global outage began at 13:42 UTC and Cloudflare-proxied domains returned HTTP 502 responses.
A single misconfigured WAF managed rule was deployed during a routine rules deployment.
A regular expression in the rule drove CPU utilization to 100 percent on machines worldwide.
At the worst point, traffic dropped by 82 percent.
The WAF rules were deployed globally in one operation rather than through the normal progressive deployment process.
Cloudflare understood the event by 14:02 UTC and a global WAF ruleset termination restored traffic at 14:09 UTC.
After reviewing and rolling back the offending rules and testing the fix, Cloudflare re-enabled the managed rulesets at 14:52 UTC.

chronosfix_inferences.summary: A progressive rollout gate could have reduced blast radius.
A catastrophic-backtracking performance test is a relevant adversarial validation candidate for WAF rule changes.

synthetic_reconstruction.reason: The source is retained as a provenance-backed public incident; no unverified production metrics are synthesized.
